description: Experience the quintessential flavors of India with our Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken. Marinated in a rich blend of yogurt and aromatic spices, this chicken is grilled to smoky perfection, resulting in tender, juicy pieces with a beautiful charred exterior. It's a delightful and authentic centerpiece for any Indian dinner.

ingredients.notes: cut into 8 pieces or boneless thighs/drumsticks

instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken
instructions.text: Wash and pat dry the chicken pieces thoroughly. Using a sharp knife, make deep gashes on the chicken pieces. This crucial step helps the marinade penetrate deep into the meat, ensuring maximum flavor.

instructions.title: First Marinade Application
instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl, combine the ginger garlic paste, fresh lemon juice, salt, and half of the Kashmiri red chili powder. Rub this aromatic mixture generously all over the chicken pieces, making sure it gets into all the gashes. Let the chicken marinate at room temperature for at least 30 minutes.

instructions.title: Prepare the Second Marinade
instructions.text: While the chicken is undergoing its first marinade, prepare the main tandoori masala. In a separate bowl, whisk together the thick Greek yogurt, the remaining red chili powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala, turmeric powder, black pepper, and the optional red or orange food color. Add the mustard oil and mix until thoroughly combined.

instructions.title: Combine and Extended Marination
instructions.text: Add the chicken from the first marinade directly into the bowl with the second yogurt-spice mixture. Ensure every piece of chicken is completely coated with the rich marinade. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for a minimum of 4 hours, or ideally overnight, for the best and most tender results.

instructions.title: Set Up the Charcoal Grill
instructions.text: Prepare your charcoal grill for direct medium-high heat. Arrange the charcoal and allow it to heat up until the coals are glowing red and covered with a light layer of ash. Clean the grill grates thoroughly with a wire brush and lightly oil them to prevent the chicken from sticking.

instructions.title: Grill the Tandoori Chicken
instructions.text: Carefully place the marinated chicken pieces directly onto the hot grill grates. Cook for approximately 25-35 minutes, turning the chicken every 5-7 minutes to ensure even cooking and beautiful char marks on all sides. The internal temperature should reach 165°F (74°C). If desired, baste with any leftover marinade or a little oil during the last few minutes of grilling.

instructions.title: Rest, Garnish, and Serve
instructions.text: Once the chicken is perfectly cooked, remove it from the grill and let it rest for 5 minutes. This allows the juices to redistribute, keeping the chicken moist. Sprinkle with a pinch of chaat masala and garnish with fresh chopped cilantro before serving hot with mint chutney, sliced onion rings, and lemon wedges.

tips: For maximum flavor and tenderness, marinate the chicken for at least 8 hours or preferably overnight. The longer the marination, the deeper the flavors will infuse.
Maintain a consistent medium-high heat on your charcoal grill. If the heat is too low, the chicken may dry out; if too high, it might burn on the outside before cooking through.
Serve your Tandoori Chicken with traditional accompaniments like cooling mint chutney, sliced red onions, and fresh lemon wedges to perfectly balance the rich, spicy flavors.
article:
Unleash the vibrant flavors of India in your own backyard with a dish that’s as iconic as it is delicious: Tandoori Chicken. While traditionally cooked in a scorching hot clay oven called a tandoor, the irresistible smoky char and tender juiciness can be perfectly replicated on your charcoal grill, making it an ideal Indian dinner recipe for any occasion. There’s nothing quite like the smoky, succulent allure of Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken. It’s a feast for the senses, from its distinctive fiery red hue to its aromatic spice profile, promising a culinary journey that’s both exciting and satisfying.

## What is Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled?

Tandoori Chicken is a celebrated North Indian dish, renowned for its vivid color, tender texture, and complex flavor. It typically involves chicken pieces marinated in yogurt and a blend of spices, then traditionally cooked at high heat in a tandoor. The yogurt acts as a tenderizer, breaking down the chicken fibers, while the spices infuse deep, aromatic notes. When we talk about Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken, we’re bringing this ancient culinary art to modern grilling.

The charcoal grill is the perfect substitute for a tandoor, providing the intense, dry heat necessary to crisp the exterior while keeping the interior moist. More importantly, the charcoal imparts that quintessential smoky flavor that is characteristic of authentic tandoor cooking. The high heat from the charcoal sears the chicken quickly, locking in juices and creating those beautiful charred bits that add layers of flavor and texture. The magic truly happens when this marinated chicken meets the intense heat of a charcoal grill, giving us the exquisite Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken. It’s a testament to how simple yet powerful techniques can transform humble ingredients into a spectacular Indian dinner.

## Ingredients You Need

Preparing an authentic Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken starts with the right ingredients, ensuring a symphony of flavors in every bite.

For the Chicken:
*   2-3 lbs bone-in, skin-on chicken pieces (thighs, drumsticks, or a mix are best)
*   2 tablespoons lemon juice
*   Salt to taste

For the Marinade:
*   1 cup plain full-fat yogurt (Greek yogurt also works, but thin it slightly)
*   2 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste (equal parts fresh ginger and garlic, minced)
*   1 tablespoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color, or regular for heat)
*   1 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 tablespoon ground cumin
*   1 tablespoon ground coriander
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 teaspoon tandoori masala (optional, but enhances flavor)
*   1/2 teaspoon black pepper
*   Red food coloring (optional, for authentic bright red color)
*   2 tablespoons mustard oil (or any neutral oil)

For Basting:
*   Melted butter or oil

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Follow these steps to create a show-stopping Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken that will impress everyone at your dinner table.

1.  **Prepare the Chicken:** Rinse the chicken pieces and pat them thoroughly dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, make 2-3 deep slits into each piece of chicken. This allows the marinade to penetrate deeply, infusing maximum flavor. Sprinkle the chicken with lemon juice and salt, rubbing it into the slits. Let sit for 15 minutes.
2.  **Make the Marinade:** In a large bowl, combine the yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric powder, ground cumin, ground coriander, garam masala, tandoori masala (if using), black pepper, and red food coloring (if desired). Mix well until all ingredients are thoroughly combined and the marinade is smooth. Stir in the mustard oil.
3.  **Marinate the Chicken:** Add the prepared chicken pieces to the marinade, ensuring each piece is completely coated. Use your hands to really work the marinade into the slits. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or ideally overnight (up to 24 hours) for the best flavor and tenderness. The longer it marinates, the more flavorful and tender your Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken will be.
4.  **Prepare the Grill:** Set up your charcoal grill for two-zone cooking: one side with direct high heat and the other with indirect medium heat. Light the charcoal and let it burn until covered with a thin layer of grey ash. This usually takes about 20-30 minutes. Clean the grill grates and oil them lightly to prevent sticking.
5.  **Grill the Chicken:** Place the marinated chicken pieces directly over the hot charcoal (direct heat zone). Sear for 2-3 minutes per side until nicely charred. This creates that beautiful crust and smoky flavor.
6.  **Move to Indirect Heat:** Once seared, move the chicken to the indirect heat zone. Close the grill lid and cook for 20-30 minutes, turning occasionally. During this time, baste the chicken frequently with melted butter or oil. Basting helps keep the chicken moist and adds a rich flavor.
7.  **Check for Doneness:** The chicken is done when its internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C) at its thickest part. The juices should run clear. If needed, move the chicken back over direct heat for a final char or to cook stubborn spots.
8.  **Rest and Serve:** Once cooked, remove the Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken from the grill and let it rest for 5-10 minutes before serving. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring tender and moist chicken.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Mastering the art of Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken involves a few key techniques that will elevate your dish from good to extraordinary.

*   **Score Deeply:** Don't be shy with the knife! Deep slits in the chicken allow the marinade to penetrate fully, ensuring flavor in every bite.
*   **Marinate Longer:** While 4 hours is good, an overnight marinade (12-24 hours) is truly transformative. The yogurt and spices have more time to work their magic, resulting in incredibly tender and flavorful chicken.
*   **Use Bone-in, Skin-on Chicken:** This yields the most flavorful and moist results. The bones add flavor, and the skin helps protect the meat from drying out, even if you discard it before eating.
*   **Control Your Heat:** A two-zone fire is crucial. Start with high direct heat for charring, then move to indirect heat for even cooking without burning. Don't overcrowd the grill, as this can lower the grill temperature and steam the chicken instead of grilling it.
*   **Baste Generously:** Regular basting with melted butter or oil not only adds flavor but also keeps the chicken moist and helps achieve that characteristic glossy finish.
*   **Don't Fear the Char:** A little char is a good thing! It adds to the authentic smoky flavor and visual appeal of Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken.
*   **Use a Meat Thermometer:** This is your best friend for perfectly cooked chicken. It eliminates guesswork and ensures your chicken is safely cooked and not overdone.

## Serving Suggestions

Serving your homemade Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken is an experience in itself, often accompanied by a variety of sides that complement its rich flavors.

*   **Naan or Roti:** Warm, fluffy naan bread or whole wheat roti are perfect for scooping up the chicken and its delicious juices.
*   **Basmati Rice:** A side of fragrant basmati rice or jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a comforting base.
*   **Raita:** A cooling yogurt dip with cucumber, mint, or boondi helps balance the spices.
*   **Mint Chutney:** A fresh, vibrant mint and coriander chutney adds a zesty kick.
*   **Onion Salad:** Thinly sliced red onions, often marinated in lemon juice and a pinch of chili powder, offer a refreshing crunch.
*   **Lemon Wedges:** A squeeze of fresh lemon juice just before eating brightens all the flavors.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken is a masterpiece, feel free to experiment with these variations and substitutions to suit your taste and dietary needs.

*   **Chicken Cuts:** If you prefer, boneless chicken thighs or breasts can be used, but adjust grilling time accordingly as they cook faster. Whole chickens can also be spatchcocked and grilled.
*   **Spice Levels:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder to your preference for heat. For a milder version, reduce the chili powder and add a bit more paprika for color.
*   **Smoked Paprika:** A teaspoon of smoked paprika can enhance the smoky flavor even further, especially if your charcoal isn't providing enough.
*   **Other Grilling Methods:** If you don't have a charcoal grill, a gas grill can be used (though you'll miss some smoky flavor). You can also finish Tandoori Chicken in a very hot oven under the broiler after searing it in a cast-iron pan.
*   **Vegetarian Tandoori:** The same marinade works wonders on paneer (Indian cheese), large mushrooms, cauliflower florets, or chunky vegetables like bell peppers and onions. Skewer them and grill until tender and lightly charred.
*   **Marinade Additions:** For an extra layer of flavor, consider adding a pinch of fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi) or a dash of black salt (kala namak) to the marinade.

Embark on a culinary adventure and bring the taste of authentic Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken to your dinner table. This Indian dinner recipe is more than just a meal; it’s an experience, a celebration of flavors, and a testament to the joy of home cooking. With a little preparation and these detailed instructions, you’ll be grilling your way to a memorable feast that will have everyone asking for seconds.
